verses.text: The contacts of the senses with external objects, O son of Kunti, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They are fleeting and impermanent; endure them with equanimity, O descendant of Bharata.
The soul is never born nor does it die; having once been, it never ceases to be. Unborn, eternal, changeless, and primeval, it is not slain when the body is slain.
Thy right is to the work alone, never to its fruits; let not the fruits of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be to inaction.
He whose mind is untroubled in the midst of sorrows, who is indifferent amid pleasures, and who is free from passion, fear, and anger, is called a sage of steadfast wisdom.

Brooding on objects of sense begets attraction; from attraction grows desire; from desire comes anger. From anger arises delusion; from delusion confusion of memory; from confusion of memory the ruin of reason; and from ruin of reason a man perishes.
Therefore, constantly perform the action which ought to be done, without attachment; for by performing action without attachment, man reaches the Supreme.
Whatsoever a great man does, that very thing other men do; whatever standard he sets up, the world follows.
Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well performed. Better is death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with peril.
Truly there is no purifier in this world like wisdom. He who is perfected in yoga finds it in his own Self in due season.
The man of faith, who is devoted and has restrained his senses, attains knowledge; and having attained knowledge, he swiftly attains supreme peace.
Let a man lift himself by his own Self, let him not debase himself; for the Self alone is the friend of the self, and the Self alone is the enemy of the self.
From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it and bring it back under the control of the Self alone.

Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, uprightness, non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, and compassion to all living beings—these are the endowments of him who is born with the divine nature.
Triple is the gate of hell, destructive of the self: lust, anger, and greed. Therefore, let a man abandon these three.
